question.question: A 65-year-old man with a longstanding history of poorly-controlled hypertension and no recent illness or cardiac disease presents to clinic complaining of chest pain that is worse on inspiration and relieved by sitting forward. Vital signs are stable. On exam, you detect a friction rub. Routine labs show K 7.5 and Cr 5.1. If this patient's clinical signs and laboratory findings are indicative of a chronic condition, what would be expected on urinary analysis?

action.justification: The pleuritic chest pain relieved by sitting forward with a friction rub suggests uremic pericarditis, supported by K 7.5 and Cr 5.1 from chronic kidney disease. CKD classically produces broad, waxy casts from chronically dilated, damaged tubules. Muddy brown granular casts suggest ATN, RBC casts glomerulonephritis, and fatty casts nephrotic syndrome.
limitations: No external evidence was supplied; the prior PubMed search returned no records, so this relies on standard clinical knowledge.

tools.name: search_pubmed
tools.description: Search PubMed for papers relevant to a clinical question or a named trial. Optional: answer directly when existing knowledge is adequate. Returns at most five real titles, publication metadata and up to 400 abstract characters, with source IDs. An excerpt may omit the needed finding. Use read_pubmed_abstract with returned numeric PMIDs to inspect more text. No full text; PubMed indexing is not quality appraisal.

tools.name: read_pubmed_abstract
tools.description: Read up to three abstracts for numeric PMIDs actually returned by this episode's PubMed searches. Returns up to 3500 characters per abstract, explicitly flagged if missing/truncated. Cite the returned source IDs; search/read IDs are distinct immutable views. Reads abstracts, not full-text articles. Do not guess IDs or assume a paper supports a claim from its title.
